gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the GardePro E8 2.0 Pro, a lookalike model of the previous generation, cannot join a home router. GardePro still sells it for $99.99, $20 less than the 3.0 Pro models, and its store listing says 'Unable to connect to home router'. Only the 3.0 Pro generation (E8 3.0 Pro, E9 3.0 Pro) joins 2.4 GHz home Wi-Fi.
standout_why: I compared against these pages. (1) The cited GardePro E8 3.0 Pro overview says 2.4 GHz home Wi-Fi and no Live View in Home WiFi mode, but it never mentions the 2.0 generation. (2) The cited Magnolia Trail Camera page says hotspot cameras in general can't join a router, names the E6 as one, and says the Link hub plugs into the router by Ethernet. It doesn't name the E8 2.0 Pro, the US/Canada-only limit, the fact that the R3 camera works only with the hub, or the solar panel lists. (3) itechguides (uncited, ranked 5th) names only the MAXDONE cameras, the GardePro E6, the Foreseen PR701W-4K and the SP350 panel for the E6. (4) The cited E9 3.0 Pro product page returned HTTP 429 to my fetch. Its store listing came through storecheck and doesn't mention the 2.0 Pro. The manuals.plus E8 2.0 Pro PDF in ChatGPT's results gave no readable text, so I couldn't check what it says.
decides: This confirms the pick: buy a GardePro model with '3.0 Pro' in the name (E8 3.0 Pro or E9 3.0 Pro, both $119.99 on gardepro.com today). Don't buy the $99.99 E8 2.0 Pro, which looks the same, because GardePro says it can't connect to a home router. If the camera is out of Wi-Fi range, go with the Link 1.0, but it has hard limits. The R3 camera works only through the Link 1.0 Hub. The Hub must be wired by Ethernet to a router with DHCP enabled. One Hub takes at most 16 cameras. The kit is sold for the US and Canada only.
